title: 1964 AHSME Problem 34
statement:
If \(n\) is a multiple of \(4,\) the sum

\[ \begin{aligned} s&=1+2i+3i^2+\cdots\\ &\quad+(n+1)i^n, \end{aligned} \]

where \(i=\sqrt{-1},\) equals:

solutions.text:
Write \(n=4m.\) For \(j=0,\ldots,m-1,\) the four terms with exponents \(4j\) through \(4j+3\) sum to \[ \begin{aligned} &(4j+1)+(4j+2)i\\ &\quad-(4j+3)-(4j+4)i\\ &=-2-2i. \end{aligned} \] The final term is \(4m+1.\) Therefore \[ \begin{aligned} s&=m(-2-2i)+(4m+1)\\ &=\frac{n+2-ni}{2}. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Group the terms in blocks of four powers of \(i\)
Each complete block beginning with coefficient \(4j+1\) sums to \(-2-2i\)
